newsitem.title: FRANCE: ENI's Bernabe warns against European "dash for gas".
newsitem.headline: ENI's Bernabe warns against European "dash for gas".

text.p: The managing director of Italian state ENI SpA sounded a warning on Thursday against the enthusiastic "dash for gas" under way in Europe.
Franco Bernabe was speaking at the Gas Executives Summit conference where a number of speakers agreed in predicting growth in European gas demand of around 150 billion cubic metres by 2010.
But Bernabe said, "I am always suspicious of consensus. All panellists agree about the growth in power generation technology, the environmental benefits, the efficiency of gas and so on.

"Italy is one country expected to have among the highest levels of growth because of oil substitution but the electricity industry has a huge number of traditional generating plants and has made big investment.
"And they have also made big environmental investments and dramatically cut emissions to meet regulations for emissions by the beginning of 1998.
"So who will take the burden of a write-off of $20 or $30 or $40 billion? The same situation applies in several other countries."
Henk Dijkgraaf, chief executive, gas and coal, at Royal Dutch/Shell Group, echoed Bernabe's comments.
"His remarKs are valid that we must beware of conventional wisdom. This can be a dangerous guide to the future," he said.
